tools.name: read_url
tools.description: URL in, clean main content out. Strips navigation, ads, cookie banners and boilerplate. Also converts PDF, DOCX, XLSX, ODT and CSV documents. Respects robots.txt. Not charged if the page cannot be read. Price 0.002 USDC per call; first 3 calls per day free.

tools.name: read_urls_batch
tools.description: Same as /read for up to 10 URLs in parallel. Charged only if at least one URL succeeds; each result reports ok or its error. Price 0.008 USDC per call; first 3 calls per day free.

tools.name: page_metadata
tools.description: Fast page metadata for link previews, crawling and source attribution. Price 0.002 USDC per call; first 3 calls per day free.

tools.name: summarize_url
tools.description: Reads the URL and returns a faithful summary plus 3-7 key points. Optional to: ta, hi, te, kn, ml, bn, mr, gu, ur, ar adds a translated summary. Price 0.005 USDC per call; first 3 calls per day free.

tools.name: ask_url
tools.description: Answers only from the page content and returns supporting quotes that are checked to appear verbatim in the page. Says found=false instead of guessing. Price 0.01 USDC per call; first 3 calls per day free.

tools.name: extract_fields
tools.description: Structured data extraction. Send a URL and the fields you want (e.g. name, price, date, email); get a JSON object with one value per field plus the exact page text that supports each value, checked to appear in the page. Missing fields come back as null instead of guessed. Works on JavaScript pages

tools.name: watch_page
tools.description: Creates a page watcher. We re-read the page every 6 hours and record what changed (lines added and removed). Optional keywords: only report changes that mention them. Optional webhook_url: we POST each change to you. Check anytime for free with GET /watch/{watch_id}; cancel with DELETE /watch/{watch

tools.name: research_question
tools.description: Finds sources (Wikipedia search, or the URLs you give), reads each one, pulls out facts with exact supporting quotes that are checked against the source, then writes a short report with numbered citations. Unverified facts are dropped. Not charged if no source can be read or nothing relevant is foun

tools.name: safe_read_url
tools.description: Reads a page like /read but first scans it for prompt injection aimed at AI agents: hidden text (display:none, zero-size or off-screen elements, HTML comments, attributes), invisible Unicode (tag-character smuggling, zero-width), base64-encoded orders, fake system/chat markers, and visible text that

tools.name: safe_check_text
tools.description: Send text, Markdown, an email body or raw HTML. Returns a risk score, every hidden or suspicious instruction aimed at AI agents (hidden HTML, invisible Unicode, encoded payloads, fake system messages, data-exfiltration or payment-redirect orders) and a cleaned version that is safer to pass to an LLM

tools.name: translate_url
tools.description: Reads the page and translates the first 4000 characters, keeping numbers, names and links unchanged. Number guard: every number and amount is checked against the source and re-translated if changed; numbers_checked reports the result. Price 0.01 USDC per call; first 3 calls per day free.

tools.name: crawl_site
tools.description: Starts at the URL and follows links on the same site (only under the same folder by default, or the whole site with scope=site), reading up to 20 pages in parallel. Returns each page's title, word count and clean Markdown. Respects robots.txt. Not charged if the start page cannot be read. Price 0.03

tools.name: extract_tables
tools.description: Finds HTML tables (handles header rows, colspan and rowspan) or Markdown tables from PDFs/Excel files, and returns them as JSON objects keyed by column header and/or CSV. Use table_index to get one table. render=true for tables built by JavaScript. Not charged if no table is found. Price 0.003 USDC

tools.name: screenshot_url
tools.description: Opens the page in a real Chrome browser, waits for it to load and returns a JPEG or PNG as base64 (MCP clients receive it as an image). Options: full_page, width, height, wait_ms. Useful for visual checks, monitoring, receipts and giving vision models a look at a page. Not charged if the page fails

tools.name: verify_claim
tools.description: Give a claim (and optionally up to 5 source URLs; otherwise Wikipedia is searched). Each source is read and judged; every quote is checked word-for-word against the page. Returns verdict (supported, contradicted, disputed, not_enough_evidence), confidence, evidence per source and a corrected claim w

tools.name: structure_to_json
tools.description: Send text (or a url) and a JSON Schema (or a simple field list). Returns data that is validated against the schema: numbers cleaned, dates as YYYY-MM-DD, enums matched, required fields checked; if the first try fails it is fixed and re-checked automatically. Each field is marked found_in_source, der

tools.name: read_invoice
tools.description: Reads an invoice, bill or receipt (text, web page, PDF or image URL) and returns vendor, customer, invoice number, dates, currency, line items, discounts, taxes, shipping, total and amount due. Then re-does the maths itself: quantity x price per line, lines vs subtotal, tax rates, subtotal + tax = t

tools.name: check_terms
tools.description: Give a site or its terms page (or paste the text). Finds the terms of service and privacy policy, reads them and flags 16 consumer risks: auto-renewal, trial converts to paid, hard to cancel, no refunds, early termination fees, price changes, hidden fees, forced arbitration, class-action waiver, dat

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_url, read_urls_batch, extract_fields, watch_page, research_question, safe_read_url, safe_check_text, crawl_site, extract_tables, screenshot_url, verify_claim, structure_to_json, read_invoice · Private data: read_url, watch_page, safe_read_url, extract_tables, read_invoice · Public sink: extract_fields, watch_page, safe_check_text, structure_to_json · Destructive: watch_page, safe_read_url.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_url, read_urls_batch, extract_fields, watch_page, research_question, safe_read_url, safe_check_text, crawl_site, extract_tables, screenshot_url, verify_claim, structure_to_json, read_invoice · Private data: read_url, watch_page, safe_read_url, extract_tables, read_invoice · Public sink: extract_fields, watch_page, safe_check_text, structure_to_json · Destructive: watch_page, safe_read_url

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
